title: /cost reports each session's own model and tokens (a follow-up is not the chain's model)
description:
## Goal

`GET /api/proxy/issues/{identifier}/cost` reports what each model actually cost a task, and how many tokens, per session. Then nobody reading it mistakes one session's model for the whole chain's.

## Context

LIN-4257's research (5 Nov) found the following.

* **All 45 implementation dispatches in the window were routed to Haiku, yet** `/cost` **labels 21 of them Opus.** The label comes from the last session in the chain. In 17 of the 21, that last session is a read-only Opus follow-up (the Survey's after-questions, sent into the builder's session after merge), so its cost is billed inside "implementation" with no way to tell the two apart.
* `/cost` already computes per-model figures, then leaves them out of the response, and it has no token counts. The nearest token source (`scripts/survey-costmix-tokens.mjs`) weights by model price, so it can't give a within-one-model comparison.

## This step

`/cost`'s response carries, per worker session, the model (or models) it ran and its tokens, alongside the existing USD. A follow-up session that resumes another session (`followUpTo`) is reported as its own row, not folded into the session it continues. Each model call is still counted once, as today; coverage and `unpriced` keep their meaning, and an unknown is never zero.

**Not this ticket:** changing how cost is attributed to issues; moving the Survey after-questions elsewhere.

## Done when

* For a ticket with a Haiku build and an Opus follow-up, `/cost` shows both sessions with their own model, tokens and USD. The sum is unchanged from today's total.
* The proxy instructions and `docs/architecture/dispatch-and-proxy.md` (or wherever `/cost` is documented) describe the new fields.
* A test fails if the label reverts to the last session's model.

## Report back

The fields added, a before/after for one real ticket from the window, and anything else in `/cost` that reads one session as the chain.

## How to go about it (from a Survey before work began)

Both Surveys (on this ticket, 12:27, at `b53917365`) found that the ticket's diagnosis is partly stale:

* a `followUpTo` row inherits its anchor's `rootItemId`, so a builder and its follow-up are **one lineage row** in `workerSessions`;
* on the records path (all post-LIN-4201 work), the label is the **cost-dominant** model (`foldRequestUsage`), not the last session's. The "last counted row" comment (`lib/cost-read.js` about 481) is true only for legacy snapshots;
* splitting `workerSessions` into one row per dispatch would quietly change readers that never call `/cost` (the Models page via `model-routing-spend.js`, the routing preview, the effort readout), which all assume one row per lineage, keyed by base kind.

The person's scope call, in order:

1. **Look at real rows first.** Take one of LIN-4257's 17 mislabelled tickets, read its raw rows, and price the build and the follow-up by hand. In the snapshot era, the last cumulative snapshot was priced at one model's rate, so a Haiku build may have been priced as Opus. If so, "the sum is unchanged" can't hold for snapshot lineages. Settle it: the sum is unchanged on the records path; snapshot-only lineages get `dispatches: null` and a note, never a guessed split.
2. **Keep** `workerSessions` **as it is, and add one nested field per lineage:** for example `dispatches: [{itemId, kind, dispatchedAt, followUpTo, byModel:[{model, requests, tokens, costUsd}], tokens, costUsd}]`, built in `summarizeReadCost` from the lineage's records grouped by posting row. Each record is counted once, so the entries sum to the lineage `costUsd`. **Check the open-0 caveat on real data:** a build that ran before the records deploy may have its records posted under a later row's `itemId` (the runner walks the whole transcript the first time it sees a session). If that happens, assign by record time against `dispatchedAt`, and say which rule you used.
3. **Expose the lineage-level** `tokens` **and** `byModel` that are already computed and then dropped.
4. **Fix the stale comment, and the two docs that actually describe** `/cost`**:** `docs/proxy-integration.md` (which says "one entry per lineage… not per dispatch row"; still true, with `dispatches` now beside it) and `lib/proxy-instructions.js`. Not `docs/architecture/dispatch-and-proxy.md`, which doesn't cover `/cost`; the ticket's pointer was wrong.
5. **The published key order is pinned** (`tests/unit/terminal-marked-task-cost.test.js:914`, LIN-4177). New keys go where that test allows, or the pin moves with a recorded reason.

**Not in this ticket:** changing the lineage label to the founder dispatch's model (it changes Models-page figures and attribution; to the tally); per-row `kind` beyond what `dispatches` shows.

## At merge (who else must learn about it)

* A test: a Haiku build plus an Opus follow-up gives two `dispatches` entries with their own models and tokens, summing to the lineage `costUsd`.
* A snapshot-only lineage gives `dispatches: null`.
* The Models page, routing preview and effort readout figures are unchanged (show it).
* Both docs describe the new fields.

## Research findings

Discharged. Preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail (research comment of 5 Nov, 12:41Z).

## Implementation Plan

Implemented as approved in [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2295](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2295>) (merged as `6ff38cf5`). `/cost` keeps one `workerSessions` row per lineage and adds `tokens`, `byModel` and `dispatches` (per-dispatch entries, `null` for lineages without records of their own). Deviations, both accepted in review: `goldens.json` was not re-recorded (a pattern entry in `expected-changes.json` covers the additive keys; `goldens-lin4197.json` was re-recorded); a dispatch with no records reads `byModel: null`. The full plan and the research findings are preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

fits one session

plan-review due: no (additive wire keys on one derived view, no guard or contract loosened, no credentials, merge rules or dispatch contract touched; the golden re-record is the only hard-to-spot part and is its own commit with a path diff).

Follow-ups for the "reads one session as the chain" class: LIN-4273 (lineage kind/model/duration on the Models page, routing typicals, effort readout) and LIN-4274 (Opus after-answer into a Haiku session costs 1.6-4.8x the build).

comments.body:
## Survey open-0: LIN-4263 @ b53917365

(LinearViewer `origin/main`, where `/cost` lives. Runner context is from simple-dispatcher @ `07c88f7a3`.)

**Why it's hard**

1. **A follow-up isn't a separate session.** A `followUpTo` resume reuses the same transcript and keeps `rootItemId`, so `workerSessions[]` has one entry per *lineage* (`lib/cost-read.js` `summarizeReadCost`). "Its own row" has to mean a dispatch row (itemId) inside a lineage, and the response has no slot for that grain yet.

2. **In the LIN-4257 window, the USD is probably wrong, not just the label.** Before 4 Nov, claude-code posted a *cumulative* `[usage]` snapshot of the whole transcript with one `model` (removed `postUsageSnapshot`, runner `44ab30e`). Harbour priced it at that one model's rate (`lib/session-telemetry.js`), and the fold keeps only the last running total (`lib/row-usage.js`). If that last snapshot is the Opus follow-up's, the Haiku build's tokens were very likely priced as Opus. In that case "sum unchanged" and "each session's own model and USD" can't both hold. A per-row split means diffing the build row's last snapshot against the follow-up's and pricing each separately, and that changes the total.

3. **The two read paths behave differently.** On the records path (from 4 Nov), the label is already the *cost-dominant* model (`foldRequestUsage`), not the last one, so Opus can still be the honest label. Records carry `itemId`, but the runner walks the whole transcript the first time it sees a session. So for a build that ran before the deploy, the build's records are posted under the follow-up's itemId. Splitting by record `at` against row `dispatchedAt` is safer than splitting by itemId.

4. **The wire shape is pinned and has consumers.** "Published keys and their order are unchanged (LIN-4177)" is asserted at `tests/unit/terminal-marked-task-cost.test.js:914`. `workerSessions` also feeds `lib/effort-readout.js`, `lib/model-routing-spend.js` (keyed on `kind`) and `routes/settings.js`. Splitting entries would shift their per-kind means. Nesting per-row detail under each lineage (`rows: [{itemId, kind, models, tokens, costUsd}]`) avoids that. `byModel` is already computed on the records path, then dropped.

5. **Snapshot rows are deleted after 2026-12-04.** Any snapshot-diffing code has a short life.

**Symptom vs cause:** The label is the symptom. The cause is that a lineage folds into one model, and in the snapshot era that also misprices it. `kind` is still the base kind, so follow-up spend counts as "implementation". That's out of scope, but per-row `kind` would make it visible.

**What I'd do first:** Take one of the 17 tickets and read its raw rows. Compare the build row's last `[usage]` (model, tokens) with the follow-up's, and reprice both by hand. If today's total turns out to be Haiku tokens at Opus rates, settle the "sum unchanged" criterion before writing the test: either it applies to the records path only, or the total gets corrected with `unpriced` kept. Then add nested per-row detail rather than reshaping `workerSessions[]`.

## Survey global: LIN-4263 @ b5391736

(LinearViewer `origin/main`. `/cost` lives there, not in simple-dispatcher.)

**Where it lands.** `routes/proxy-compute.js` (`/cost`, about 40 lines that only fetch) over `lib/cost-read.js` `summarizeReadCost`, which reads `lib/request-usage-fold.js`. This area is getting better, and fast. LIN-4177→4226 turned it into "one cost read", with an explicit figure rule (null, never a partial). The legacy snapshot path is marked for deletion after 2026-12-04, and there have been about 15 commits here in two weeks. The task should land on the shape that is still settling, not on an older one.

**The ticket's diagnosis is partly stale.** In `/cost`, a `workerSessions` row is a **lineage** (keyed by `rootItemId`). A `followUpTo` row inherits its anchor's `rootItemId` (`lib/dispatch-factory.js:720`), so the builder and the Survey follow-up are one row. On record lineages (all post-LIN-4201 work), the `model` label is the **cost-dominant** model (`foldRequestUsage` `last.model`), not the last session's. The "last counted row" comment at `cost-read.js:481` is true only for legacy snapshots. An Opus follow-up wins the label because it outspends the Haiku build. Tokens (`fold.tokens`) and `byModel` are already computed and then dropped at `summarizeReadCost`. Records carry `itemId` (the posting row), so a per-dispatch split is cheap: group a lineage's records by `itemId` and run `foldRequestUsage` on each group. Each record is still counted once, so the sum equals the lineage `costUsd`.

**Done the obvious way** (`workerSessions` becomes one row per dispatch):
- It would break readers who don't call `/cost` at all. `workerSessions` is shared with the Models page (`model-routing-spend.js` `agentSpendByJob`/`typicalByModel`, through `model-routing-history.js`), the routing preview (`routes/dispatch.js:696`), and the effort readout (`effort-readout.js`, mean duration per kind). All of these assume one row per lineage, keyed by the base kind. Splitting the rows would quietly change "typical cost per implementation run", and no test watches that meaning.
- The docs say the opposite of the change: `docs/proxy-integration.md` ("one entry per lineage… not per dispatch row") and `lib/proxy-instructions.js` (about line 360). `docs/architecture/dispatch-and-proxy.md` doesn't document `/cost` at all, so it's the wrong place to edit. The ticket names it as a fallback. The figure tests (`proxy-issue-cost-route`, `cost-read*`, `lin-4201-*`) pin the current shape.
- The word "session" would get a third meaning. It already means a Claude `sessionId` (which the builder and the follow-up *share*, because a follow-up resumes) and a lineage (`workerSessions`).

**What leaves it better, within this task's budget:** keep `workerSessions` as it is and add one nested field per lineage, e.g. `dispatches: [{itemId, kind, dispatchedAt, followUpTo, byModel:[{model, requests, tokens, costUsd}], tokens, costUsd}]`, built in `summarizeReadCost` from records grouped by `itemId`. For a snapshot-only lineage, use `dispatches: null` (cumulative snapshots can't be split, and unknown must not read as zero). Expose lineage-level `tokens`/`byModel` too, since they already exist. Fix the comment at `cost-read.js:481`, update both docs that describe `/cost`, and add a test: Haiku build + Opus follow-up gives two dispatch entries with their own models, and they sum to the lineage `costUsd`.

**Better still, but not this task's:** the label itself. Readers that want "the model this job ran on" (the Models page, routing typicals) should read the founder dispatch's model rather than the lineage's cost-dominant one. Changing that changes Models-page figures and attribution, so it's a separate ticket. The 2026-12-04 snapshot deletion will also make "records only" true and remove the `dispatches: null` case.

## Research: LIN-4263 @ LinearViewer `b5391736`, simple-dispatcher `07c88f7`

Read-only, apart from this comment, the description and the status. A throwaway spike ran in a scratch worktree, which was then removed; nothing was pushed. `/cost` and dispatch rows were read 12:35–12:55 UTC on 5 Nov. Transcripts and runner state were read from this host (`~/.claude/projects`, `simple-dispatcher/state/sessions.json`).

**Staleness check.** `git log --since=2026-11-05T12:21:32Z` is empty for `lib/`, `routes/`, `docs/` and `tests/` in LinearViewer, so HEAD is the Surveys' base.

### 1. Real rows first (the person's step 1): the sum holds on the records path

I priced 14 of the window's "Survey 1a (after)" lineages by hand. Each one is the builder's transcript plus its subagent files, walked with the runner's own `walkRequestRecords` (`simple-dispatcher/request-usage.js`) and priced with `priceRequest` (`lib/model-pricing.js`). I split each one at the follow-up's dispatch or resume time.

| Ticket | `/cost` lineage (label, USD) | Hand total | Build (Haiku) | Follow-up (Opus) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LIN-4252 | opus, 3.02716297 | 3.02716297 | 63 req, $0.890 | 6 req, $2.137 |
| LIN-4234 | opus, 2.30615921 | 2.30615921 | 58 req, $0.566 | 8 req, $1.740 |
| LIN-4239 | opus, 3.29302673 | 3.29302673 | 91 req, $1.106 | 6 req, $2.188 |
| LIN-4240 | opus, 1.46128236 | 1.46128236 | 43 req, $0.288 | 5 req, $1.174 |
| LIN-4241 | opus, 2.65951081 | 2.65951081 | 65 req, $0.712 | 6 req, $1.947 |
| LIN-4242 | opus, 3.95945169 | 3.95945169 | 104 req, $1.444 | 6 req, $2.515 |
| LIN-4243 | opus, 3.11079878 | 3.11079878 | 95 req, $1.047 | 6 req, $2.064 |
| LIN-4151 | opus, 2.36487361 | 2.36487361 | 69 req, $0.661 | 6 req, $1.704 |
| LIN-4048 | opus, 1.37865805 | 1.37865805 | 40 req, $0.238 | 5 req, $1.141 |
| LIN-4143 | opus, 3.26623897 | 3.26623897 | 88 req, $0.945 | 7 req, $2.322 |
| LIN-4248 | opus, 3.66801146 | 3.66801146 | 131 req, $1.313 | 6 req, $2.355 |
| LIN-4247 | opus, 2.34236973 | 2.34236973 | 78 req, $0.699 | 5 req, $1.643 |
| LIN-4253 | opus, 3.84871444 | 3.84871444 | 111 req, $1.375 | 7 req, $2.474 |
| LIN-4251 | opus, 4.13232478 | 4.13232478 | 126 req, $1.587 | 7 req, $2.546 |

(The Opus columns where my split point was the transcript's prompt fetch showed "2 Opus requests before the split". Those 2 are the follow-up's own first turn, the resume that fetches the prompt, so they belong to the follow-up. With the row's `dispatchedAt` as the split point, every Opus request lands in the follow-up; LIN-4252 was checked both ways.)

What this shows:
- **"Sum unchanged" holds exactly** on all 14 (to about 1e-15). Every one is a records-era lineage, and the build ran after the records runner went live (`9478e1c`, 2026-11-04T04:59Z). So the person's call stands: records-path sums are unchanged, and a split can only reallocate them.
- **The Opus label is honest, not "last session".** The follow-up is cost-dominant in every case, at 62–83% of the lineage, for only 5–8 requests. The money is the first Opus request after the resume, which writes the whole Haiku-built context into the 1h cache at Opus rates (LIN-4252: 225,251 cache-creation tokens). So the LIN-4257 reading ("routed Haiku, labelled Opus") is true, but its cause is not the label rule. The follow-up really did cost more than the build. That is a finding for the Survey loop itself: an Opus after-answer resumed into a Haiku session costs 1.6–4.8× the build it asks about.
- **Snapshot era:** confirmed that an old `[usage]` snapshot carried cumulative tokens with the *last-seen* model (`simple-dispatcher` `transcript.js` `walkUsage` at `44ab30e^`, "last-seen model wins"), priced at that one rate (`lib/session-telemetry.js` → `computeUsageCostUsd`). A snapshot-only lineage with an Opus follow-up therefore priced its Haiku build at Opus rates. That cannot be split, so `dispatches: null` there (step 2 of the scope call) is right. None of the 14 above is snapshot-only.
- **Pre-deploy candidates (open-0's caveat), named:** LIN-4197 (root `c1d71260`): a 5-beat build 01:44–02:14Z on 4 Nov, before the records runner, then a "Survey 1a (round 3)" follow-up `9879e58d` at 05:50Z. LIN-4177 (root `b6b15c91`): build 3 Nov 22:25Z, follow-ups at 01:21Z and 21:05Z on 4 Nov. LIN-4196 (root `70e909e8`): build 01:39Z on 4 Nov. Their transcripts are not on this host, so I could not price them. The runner ledger is per runner session (`request-usage-flush.js:159-162`), and the session is first seen at the post-deploy follow-up, so every record of the build is first posted under the follow-up's itemId. The upsert keeps the first poster's `itemId` (`$setOnInsert`, `lib/request-usage-store.js:10-17`). This also explains LIN-4257's "3 Opus lineages with no follow-up I could find" (LIN-4197/4198/4199): the follow-up exists and is named "Survey 1a (round 3)", not "(after)".

### 2. Corrections to the ticket, Surveys and brief (each verified)

1. **The "pinned key order" test is not `/cost`'s.** `tests/unit/terminal-marked-task-cost.test.js:909-915` (LIN-4129) pins `computeTerminalMarkedTaskCost`'s output, the `/kpis` cost block. Nothing pins `/cost`'s key order by name. The real pins on the `/cost` wire are the **replay goldens**, which serialize the S1 route body:
   - `tests/fixtures/cost-replay/goldens.json` + `expected-changes.json`, asserted by `tests/unit/cost-read.test.js:213-224` (W9: "no unlisted difference");
   - `goldens-lin4197.json`, asserted exactly (`diffReplay(...) == []`) by `tests/unit/cost-lin4197-replay.test.js:41-60`;
   - `lin4201-change-list.json`, asserted both ways by `tests/unit/lin-4201-replay-change-list.test.js` (it includes "snapshot-only reads are unchanged" and "existing corpus does not move at all").
2. **The route strips by destructuring, not by listing keys** (`routes/proxy-compute.js:744`): `({ telemetry, incomplete, ...session }) => session`. So any field added in `summarizeReadCost` reaches the wire automatically, with no route change.
3. **`foldRequestUsage`'s `byModel` has no tokens** (`lib/request-usage-fold.js:122-128`: `model, requests, pricedRequests, pricedUsd, costUsd`). The shape the brief proposes, `byModel:[{model, requests, tokens, costUsd}]`, needs the fold to sum tokens per model.
4. **The identity rows carry no `followUpTo`** (`LINEAGE_IDENTITY_PROJECTION`, `lib/dispatch-store.js:271`). A dispatch entry for a true member that the 30-day fetch did not return (a straddler) would have no `followUpTo`.
5. **The docs are staler than the ticket says.** `docs/proxy-integration.md:1238-1242` and `lib/proxy-instructions.js:384-386` justify "once per lineage" by *cumulative snapshots on every Stop*, which stopped at LIN-4203 (`44ab30e`). `routes/proxy-compute.js:627-629` says the same. `lib/cost-read.js:471` ("labels come from the lineage's last counted row") is true only for snapshot lineages; for records the label comes from `foldRequestUsage` (cost-dominant model, latest record's effort and harness; `request-usage-fold.js:20-23,117-121`).

### 3. Per-layer audit

**L1 · The fold (`lib/request-usage-fold.js`).** It prices each record once (`priceRequest`, `:83`) and gives completeness `complete|unpriced|no-usage` (`:101-103`). The label is the cost-dominant priced model (`:105-107,119`); `byModel` is ordered by priced cost (`:122`). **Must hold:** a per-dispatch figure reuses this fold on the dispatch's records, so a dispatch's completeness, unpriced rule and label rule match the lineage's. Adding `tokens` per model is additive: its only reader is `combineFolds` (`cost-read.js:195,211`), which reads `pricedUsd` only.

**L2 · The read core (`lib/cost-read.js`).** `lineageRecordsOverRecords` already hands each lineage record `members` (fetched rows, which carry `followUpTo`), `missing` (true members not fetched; identity scalars only), `requests` (this lineage's records, each with `itemId` and `at`) and `fold` (`:341-366`). `summarizeReadCost` builds `workerSessions` in four branches (no-usage `:448`, unreadable `:453`, incomplete `:461`, priced `:472`). **Must hold:** every branch emits the new keys, null when unknown and never `[]` or `0`. A record lineage is never `incomplete` (`request-usage-fold.js:24-27`, `missingRowsCanChangeFigure: false`), so splitting the priced branch's records covers every records lineage. `fold.source` is `'records'`, `'records+snapshots'` (`combineFolds`, `:203`) or absent (snapshot fold).

**L3 · The record store and loader (`lib/request-usage-store.js`, `lib/request-usage-loader.js`).** `listForAnchors` reads records by the posting row (`itemId ∈ history members of the anchor`, `:290-298`) and folds to one record per requestId; metadata, `itemId` included, comes from the earliest document (`oneRecordPerRequest`, `:159-177`). **So every record has exactly one `itemId`, and that `itemId` is a true member of the lineage.** Grouping by `itemId` is a partition: each record is counted once and the groups sum to the lineage. No new read is needed.

**L4 · The producer (simple-dispatcher `request-usage-flush.js`).** It posts to `/api/dispatch/usage/:itemId` with `session.itemMetadata.itemId` (`:118,171`), and the runner overwrites `itemMetadata` with the follow-up's at resume (seen in `sessions.json` for LIN-4252: `itemMetadata.itemId = a55d7b45`, the follow-up). The ledger (`requestLedger`, requestId → fingerprint) persists across the resume, so a records-era build's records are already acknowledged under the build's itemId before the follow-up starts. **A ledger reset or a first sight after the deploy puts earlier requests under a later itemId.** That is why the time rule (below) is needed. Not this ticket: changing the producer.

**L5 · The route and wire (`routes/proxy-compute.js:649-748`).** It fetches own rows, siblings and identity, calls `readCost`, and strips `telemetry`/`incomplete` by destructuring (`:744`). **Must hold:** no route change is needed beyond passing the opt-in (below). The 30-day `since` bound on fetched rows means `members` can omit old rows. Those come through `missing` without `followUpTo` (correction 4).

**L6 · The shared in-process readers (bystanders).** `lib/model-routing-history.js:37` (`readCost`, one call; its `workerSessions` feed the Models page `agentSpendByJob`/`typicalByModel`, `lib/model-routing-spend.js:60-76`, and the routing preview, `routes/dispatch.js:696-697`, `routes/settings.js:307-326`) and `lib/effort-readout.js:444-566` (per-kind cost, duration mean and effort distribution). Every one filters by `kind` and reads `costUsd`, `model`, `effort` and `durationMs`. None reads unknown keys, so additive fields leave their figures identical (spike: `model-routing-history.test.js` and `lin-4201-cost-callers.test.js` green). **They would pay for building `dispatches`:** one extra `foldRequestUsage` per dispatch group re-prices every record. The Models read covers the whole 30-day workspace (LIN-4200 measured about 230k records at steady state). So `dispatches` must be opt-in, built only for `/cost`.

**L7 · The KPI paths (`lib/kpi-stats.js:1087`, `lib/workspace-kpi-stats.js:181`).** They call `lineageRecords`, not `readCost`/`summarizeReadCost`, and read `record.fold`. They are untouched by a change in `summarizeReadCost`; the only change they see is the additive `byModel[].tokens` inside `fold`.

**L8 · The run page (`lib/run-view.js`, `lineageFigureOf`).** It has its own per-lineage figure over loops (S13). It does not read `workerSessions`. Untouched. The S1 = S13 agreement (`cost-read-agreement.test.js:66-90`) compares `costUsd` only and stays green.

**L9 · The pins (tests and goldens).** See correction 1. Spike result: 7 of 152 tests in the cost suites fail, **all of them replay-golden equality pins**. Every differing path is `S1.<issue>.body.workerSessions.<root>.{tokens|byModel|dispatches}`, a key present on one side only. No figure path moved. The route test, agreement, callers, records-first and Models-history tests pass unchanged.

**L10 · The docs.** `docs/proxy-integration.md:1208-1242` (the example JSON and the "Lineage de-duplication" bullet), `lib/proxy-instructions.js:352-392` (the `/cost` catalog entry; the gate prose at `:375-380` is pinned by `tests/unit/lin-2253-instructions-cost-gate-prose.test.js:80`, so that sentence must stay byte-compatible), the route header `routes/proxy-compute.js:622-648` and the comment `lib/cost-read.js:471`. Not `docs/architecture/dispatch-and-proxy.md` (confirmed: it does not cover `/cost`).

**L11 · Off-repo consumers of the `/cost` wire.** `scripts/survey-*-analyse.mjs`, `scripts/survey-effort-fetch.mjs` and `scripts/eval/jev-progress-eval.mjs` read `workerSessions[].{model,costUsd,durationMs,harness,rootItemId}` by name. Additive keys are harmless.

### 4. Options for the split rule (the person's step 2 caveat)

- **A. By posting `itemId` only.** This is exact for every records-era lineage where the build was flushed before the follow-up (all 14 above). On a pre-deploy build (LIN-4197/4177/4196) it puts the whole build into the follow-up and reports "Survey after-answer: 300 Haiku requests". That is wrong, and it reads as a fact.
- **B. By time only** (each record to the latest member with `dispatchedAt ≤ record.at`). This is right in both cases above. Its risk: a member dispatched while an earlier member's session is still writing would steal the tail of the earlier member's records (queue delay; parallel lineage members such as wakes). It ignores the posting row even when that row is credible.
- **C. Recommended: `itemId` unless it is provably late.** Keep the posting row, *unless* `record.at < postingRow.dispatchedAt`. A row cannot have made a request before it was dispatched, so that record was posted late by a later row. Only then reassign it to the latest member with `dispatchedAt ≤ record.at` (fall back to the posting row when no member qualifies, or when `at` or `dispatchedAt` is missing). This never overrides a credible posting row, fixes exactly the pre-deploy and ledger-reset shape, and needs no new data. Spiked: both shapes give two entries, Haiku build and Opus follow-up, summing to the lineage `costUsd`.

### 5. Feasibility spike (scratch worktree, removed; 86-line diff)
- `foldRequestUsage`: `byModel[].tokens` via `sumTokens` per model.
- `summarizeReadCost`: on the priced branch, `tokens: fold.tokens`; `byModel` when `fold.source === 'records'`, else null; `dispatches` built from `record.members ∪ record.missing`, records grouped by rule C, each group folded by `foldRequestUsage`.
- Synthetic Haiku build + Opus follow-up, in both shapes ("posted by own rows" and "all posted by the follow-up, earlier `at`"): two entries (`implementation`, Haiku, 2 req; `custom`, `followUpTo: b`, Opus, 1 req) summing to the lineage `costUsd` exactly.
- The cost suites: 145 pass and 7 fail, all goldens (L9).

### 6. Things in `/cost` that still read one session as the chain (the ticket's "report back")
Each is per lineage; `dispatches` makes each one visible but does not change it. This ticket changes none of them.
1. `model` / `effort` / `harness`: the lineage's cost-dominant model, and the latest record's effort and harness. `effort` is the follow-up's effort.
2. `kind` = the base kind, so the Opus after-answer counts as `implementation` spend in the Models page (`agentSpendByJob` filters `kind`; `typicalByModel` groups by the lineage `model`, so "implementation on Opus" typicals are mostly after-answers) and in the effort readout's per-kind cost.
3. `durationMs` runs from the base dispatch to lineage completion, so it includes the wait for, and the run of, the follow-up (LIN-4252 implementation: `durationMs` 3,049,093, about 50.8 min, runs from 10:28:40 to the lineage's completion at 11:19:29, after the follow-up dispatched at 11:18:32). It feeds the effort readout's per-kind mean duration.
4. `dispatchedAt` = the fetched earliest member's (plan decision ii, `cost-read.js:429-433`).

### Attack on this audit
- **A missed `workerSessions` reader?** `grep -rnE "readCost\(|lineageRecords\(|workerSessions" lib routes public scripts server.js` lists exactly L5–L8 and L11. `public/` has none. No other module imports `summarizeReadCost` (it is not exported).
- **A missed pin?** `grep -rn "workerSessions" tests/unit` names 12 files. The only whole-object assertions are `deepEqual(..., [])` (empty, unaffected) and the replay goldens (L9). The spike ran the affected suites.
- **Would the set be wrong if** a record's `itemId` could name a row outside its lineage? It cannot: `listForAnchors` reads only `itemId ∈ members(anchor)` (`request-usage-store.js:290-298`).
- **Not verified:** the pre-deploy lineages' real record `itemId`s (server-side data). The implementer should read one (e.g. LIN-4197 `/cost` before and after) and check that rule C puts the beats' records on the beats.

### Surface Assessment
`Surface Assessment: [lands cleanly]`

`dispatches` is a derived view over the records the lineage already holds, folded by the same `foldRequestUsage`. It is not a second representation: no new store, type or source of truth, and no new read. `workerSessions` keeps one row per lineage. The work consists of an opt-in flag on `readCost`, additive keys, two doc edits and goldens re-recorded with a stated reason. Bystander tax: `byModel[].tokens` adds one `sumTokens` pass per lineage for every records reader (an O(records) addition, no pricing). `dispatches` costs nothing outside `/cost` because it is opt-in. One small companion edit is optional: add `followUpTo: 1` to `LINEAGE_IDENTITY_PROJECTION` so a straddler's out-of-window members carry it (one scalar per identity row). Without it, those entries show `followUpTo: null` (unknown), which is acceptable until straddlers with records exist (from about 4 Dec).

## LIN-4263: implementation done, PR open

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2295 (branch `feat/lin-4263-cost-per-dispatch`, 3 commits: 2ac83dd7, d73f3dda, 878e6d63)

**What changed.** `/cost` keeps one `workerSessions` row per lineage and adds `tokens`, `byModel` (records lineages) and `dispatches`: one entry per dispatch with its own models, tokens and USD. Entries sum to the lineage totals. `dispatches` is `null` for snapshot-only lineages and is built only by `/cost` (`perDispatch`).

**Evidence.**
- Replay at HEAD vs branch: 12,057 differing paths, all `workerSessions.*.{tokens,byModel,dispatches}`; zero figure paths moved.
- New tests: `tests/unit/lin-4263-cost-per-dispatch.test.js` (19), including a label guard (expensive Haiku build + cheaper later Opus follow-up stays Haiku). Mutation runs: label reverted, rule C removed, flag ignored, each caught by its test.
- Unit suite 23,545 pass; hermetic keyed 23,545 pass; secret scan clean.
- CI on the PR: all checks pass (unit tests, E2E shards 1-4, secret scan, `CI success`).

**Not verified.** Real pre-deploy lineages (LIN-4197, LIN-4177, LIN-4196) and a real before/after `/cost` read: transcripts are not on this host. The late-post rule is covered by a fixture only.

**Judgment calls.** `goldens.json` (LIN-4177 baseline) not re-recorded; its change list gets a pattern entry for the additive keys. `goldens-lin4197.json` re-recorded in its own commit (additive only). A no-record dispatch reads `byModel: null`.

Awaiting review; merge is not done here.

## Review — LIN-4263

PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2295, head `878e6d63` (2ac83dd7 code + tests, d73f3dda goldens, 878e6d63 docs). Base `b5391736`. It merges cleanly with `origin/main` (`88d9607f`), and no commit on main since the base touches the PR's files.

CI: green on `878e6d63` (Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan, CI success).

**Scope against the plan.** The scope matches. The 11 files touched are the plan's places: the fold, `cost-read`, the projection, the route flag, the 2 docs plus the route header and comment, the goldens and the new test file. `docs/architecture/dispatch-and-proxy.md` is correctly left untouched. There are two deviations, both recorded in the implementation comment, and I accept both:
- `goldens.json` is not re-recorded. Instead, `expected-changes.json` gains a `pattern` entry anchored to `workerSessions.<root>.(tokens|byModel|dispatches)`, and W9 learns to read patterns. The pattern can only match keys that the LIN-4177 golden doesn't have, so it can't hide a figure move. `goldens-lin4197.json` still pins the new values exactly.
- A dispatch with no records reads `byModel: null`, not the plan's `[]`. This follows the "unknown is null" rule.

**Regression check.** I read the last 15 commits on `cost-read.js`, `request-usage-fold.js` and `proxy-compute.js` (LIN-4226, 4203, 4201, 4179, 4178, 4177, 4147).
- The LIN-2830 label rule is kept for snapshot lineages; only the comment changed.
- The LIN-4177 "scalar-only" projection stays scalar (`followUpTo` is a scalar).
- Nothing reverted earlier is re-applied.

**Tests I ran myself** on the PR head: 50 cost-area files (`lin-4263-*`, `cost-*`, `lin-4201*`, `model-routing*`, `proxy-issue-cost*`, `effort-readout*`, `request-usage*`, `*kpi*`, `terminal-marked-task-cost`, `lin-2253` gate prose). 833 tests ran and all 833 passed. The Models page, routing preview and effort readout suites are green with no changes. One test asserts that every non-`dispatches` figure is identical with the flag on and off.

**Mutation checks** (each reverted afterwards; the worktree was clean before I removed it):

**Isolated, or one of a class?** The class is "fields that read one session as the chain". Research listed its members: lineage `model`/`effort`/`harness`, `kind` as the base kind, `durationMs` and `dispatchedAt`. All of them are outside this ticket's scope, which explicitly excludes relabelling and attribution. `dispatches` makes each of them visible. Close-out files them as follow-ups if they aren't already filed. Within the bounded classes:
- All 4 `summarizeReadCost` branches emit the new keys.
- All 3 golden sets are handled.
- All 4 doc targets are edited.
- Every `workerSessions` reader reads named fields, and its suites are green.

I found no unhandled instance inside a bounded class.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside** (Done-when: "a test fails if…"; class: the per-dispatch split): dispatch order with an out-of-window, older member. **Before the merge:** close-out adds a test to `tests/unit/lin-4263-cost-per-dispatch.test.js`, under "a dispatch the fetch did not return". Setup: `fetchedRows: [f1]` (follow-up, 2h ago, `followUpTo: 'b1'`); `identityRows` hold `b1` (implementation, 5h ago) and `f1`; records `q1` (Haiku, 4h ago, `itemId: 'f1'`) and `o1` (Opus, 1h ago, `itemId: 'f1'`). The distinguishing condition: the test goes red when the `.sort((a, b) => rankOf(a) - rankOf(b))` line in `dispatchesOf` is removed.

After the deploy, re-read it. ### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

The deliverable meets the Done-when on the records path, the shape is additive, other readers are unaffected, and the load-bearing tests went red under mutation. Before the merge, close-out adds the dispatch-order test and makes the docs' null-case wording precise. After the deploy, it runs the two before/after reads above.

## Close-out — LIN-4263

**Merged:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2295, squash commit `6ff38cf5` on `main`, pinned with `--match-head-commit ed00e4e9`. `/cost` keeps one `workerSessions` row per lineage and adds `tokens`, `byModel` and `dispatches` (each dispatch with its own models, tokens and USD; `null` for lineages without records of their own).

**Changes I made after the approval** (review's Approve with a ledger; commit `ed00e4e9`):
1. Dispatch-order test, answering review's first "Inside" item. `tests/unit/lin-4263-cost-per-dispatch.test.js`, "an out-of-window older build is listed before the in-window follow-up", with review's exact setup (`fetchedRows: [f1]`, `identityRows` b1 + f1, q1 Haiku at 4h and o1 Opus at 1h both under `f1`; asserts `[['b1',1],['f1',1]]`). Mutation check: with the `.sort(rankOf)` line in `dispatchesOf` removed, this test goes red (15 pass, 1 fail); restored, 16 pass.
2. Docs null-case wording, answering review's second item. `lib/proxy-instructions.js` and `docs/proxy-integration.md` now list "snapshot-only, records plus snapshots, no usage or unreadable", and the docs say "null tokens, byModel and cost". `lin-2253-instructions-cost-gate-prose` re-run: green. Cost-area suites (`lin-4263-*`, `cost-*`, `lin-4201*`, `proxy-issue-cost*`, `lin-2253`): 247 of 247 pass.

**CI:** exists. All checks green on `ed00e4e9`, the commit merged (Unit tests, E2E shards 1-4, Secret scan, CI success; run 42033699248).

**Ledger**

LIN-4264 was already closed as a duplicate. Archive: pre-prune snapshot `84eab4ae` (13:10:43Z) confirmed equal to the pre-prune description before the description was pruned.

## Survey 1a (round 3)

**1. Why was it difficult?** The code was not the hard part. `dispatchesOf` and the new keys took about 120 lines, mostly decided by the plan. The change bound on the replay pins. Three golden sets assert whole-object equality on the S1 route body, so adding three keys fans out to ~12,000 differing paths. The real difficulty was telling "my additive keys" from "figures that moved". I lost time because `goldens.json` is already stale against HEAD (the LIN-4177 change list a–d encodes that). My first golden-vs-branch diff showed `LIN-8 pricedUsd 0.4 → 0` and I chased it as my bug. Only a HEAD-replay-vs-branch-replay diff settled it: 12,057 paths, all additive, zero figures.

**2. What I'd have done first.** Dump the replay at HEAD before touching anything, and diff branch against that, never against the goldens. I'd also have read how the three pins relate: `goldens.json` is a baseline plus a change list, `goldens-lin4197.json` is a live recording, and `lin4201-change-list.json` is an exact path set between two replays.

**3. What I'd tidy.**
- Re-baseline `goldens.json`. A golden that HEAD no longer reproduces makes every future change pay my detour.
- The W9 `pattern` entry is a special case I added so I wouldn't erase LIN-4177's list. It works, but it's a second kind of change-list entry.
- `dispatchesOf` could sit beside `foldRequestUsage` rather than in `cost-read.js`.
- `postingKeysOf` repeats `isPostingRow`'s id shapes.

**4. The ticket, if the area were how I'd want it.** "Add `dispatches` to `/cost`": one function in the read and one test file. For that, the replay pins would assert figure paths (costs, counts, labels) and leave new keys to their own tests. Then an additive field would cost nothing in the goldens.

**5. What the ticket or plan got wrong.** The surveys and research had already corrected the original diagnosis (cost-dominant, not last-session), the doc target and the key-order pin. The plan's remaining miss was "re-record the 3 golden sets". `goldens.json` can't be re-recorded without emptying the LIN-4177 change list, and `lin4201-change-list.json` is a path list, not a golden. The plan also gave a no-record dispatch `byModel: []`, while the brief said never `[]`. I chose `null`.

**6. What it left behind.**
- *Two places:* the split rule is now described in four (docs/proxy-integration.md, lib/proxy-instructions.js, the route header, the `dispatchesOf` JSDoc). `byModel` has two shapes: the fold's, with `pricedRequests`/`pricedUsd`, and the wire's, through `modelRowOf`.
- *New, without an obvious home:* `readCost`'s `perDispatch` flag, a mode where one reader gets a different row shape. Also `followUpTo` in `LINEAGE_IDENTITY_PROJECTION`, which only `/cost` reads.
- *Should have learned and didn't:* the Models page and effort readout still count an Opus after-answer as "implementation" spend. `dispatches` now makes that visible, but they don't use it. The `survey-*-analyse.mjs` scripts could read `dispatches` instead of splitting transcripts by hand.
- *Simpler:* the stale "cumulative snapshot on every Stop" rationale is gone from the docs, and the `cost-read.js` label comment now says what records lineages actually do.
